observations.source_fact: The four-line module is an index export for the Realm Carver cartridge.
observations.interpretation: This is a cartridge registration/export surface; it does not by itself establish runtime mechanics.

observations.source_fact: The page dynamically imports RealmCarverGame, fetches /api/v1/games/realm-carver/sentences?locale={locale}, takes the first returned sentence, splits sentence.term on spaces into word items, and posts xp/accuracy to /api/v1/games/realm-carver/complete on completion.
observations.interpretation: The historical page wires sentence retrieval and completion reporting around the game component.

observations.source_fact: The completion route exports POST from createCompleteRoute().
observations.interpretation: The route delegates completion handling to the shared game API factory.

observations.source_fact: The sentences route exports GET from createSentencesRoute(SAMPLE_SENTENCES).
observations.interpretation: The historical route supplies the shared sentence endpoint with SAMPLE_SENTENCES.

observations.source_fact: The test suite renders RealmCarverGame with The/cat vocabulary and covers title rendering, start-to-playing transition, HUD rendering, input/game progression, completion callback behavior, and restart rendering.
observations.interpretation: These are historical test assertions, not independent proof that the assertions matched shipped runtime behavior.

observations.source_fact: The component has start/playing/ended phases, creates state from sentences, applies directional input through tickRealmCarver, changes to ended on victory or defeat, and reports xp and accuracy once after completion.
observations.interpretation: The historical component contains a stateful play loop and terminal reporting path.

observations.source_fact: The rendered historical UI names the game Realm Carver, instructs the player to enclose words to capture them in order and return to a claimed area to finish the circuit, and renders HUD values, target word, wild/claimed/trail cells, words, monsters, player, and victory/defeat results.
observations.interpretation: These strings and render branches are historical UI/source observations; they do not establish final product requirements.
The historical component directory exposed the game component through its index.
